sections.h2: Three ways to sell in Raymore
sections.html:
People selling here can sign with an agent, advertise the house on their own, or request a bid from someone paying cash. Agents tend to net the best price for a house in good condition. A cash bid gives up part of that price and buys you speed, with no showings to schedule.

Raymore lies in Cass County and belongs to the Kansas City metro area. The 2020 census found 22,941 residents, the July 1, 2025 estimate is 26,633, and between July 2022 and July 2023 no other Missouri city grew faster. New construction nearby means a resale home is often priced against brand-new houses.

  • An agent fits a move-in ready house and an owner who can wait for a buyer's loan to clear.
  • A private sale fits someone with the hours to take calls and manage a contract.
  • A cash bid fits a house that is empty, inherited or overdue for maintenance, or a seller facing a job move or a lender's deadline.

The Raymore-Peculiar R-II School District covers the whole city, so school questions have one answer. The mean trip to work is 25.7 minutes, and the city spans about 17 square miles. Describe the drive from your street to Route 58, since commute time weighs on buyers here.

Census counts from 2020 show 8,844 housing units, 4.5% of them vacant. Buyers therefore have choices, and they will ask for paperwork. A discount of even a tenth off a $339,100 home is a large sum, so compare what each offer leaves after costs.

City Hall stands at 100 Municipal Circle, just south of Route 58. The Development Services office takes permit submissions, schedules inspections and answers questions about contractor licensing, decks, fences and swimming pools. Call the main line at (816) 892-3015, the Building Official at (816) 892-3009 or the Building Inspector at (816) 892-3010.

Request the permit history for any finished space, roof replacement or addition ahead of listing. If a past project never got a final sign-off, resolving it now is easier than doing it with a buyer waiting.

Development Services also runs code enforcement. The property maintenance code in Chapter 545 is the part sellers meet most.

  • Grass and weeds may reach 8 inches on a developed lot and 12 inches on an undeveloped one, and poison ivy, oak or sumac counts as a violation.
  • Garbage, discarded furniture and appliances, stored construction materials and loose brush are nuisances under Section 545.445.
  • A vehicle on private property is inoperable if it has no valid plate or decal, flat tires, missing parts or dismantled pieces.
  • Signs may not stand in the right-of-way, which includes the strip between street and sidewalk.

The city also requires registration of foreclosed properties. If you are unsure about a complaint at your address, call the Code Enforcement Officer at (816) 892-3027 or read the code enforcement page. Development Services posts guides on fences, decks, pools, accessory buildings, sump pump discharge and radon control systems.

sections.h2: Property tax due dates and proration
sections.html:
Tax bills from the county Collector go out in November and are payable through December 31. For a mailed check, the U.S. postmark date counts. Paying late can add penalties and fees of up to 25% in the first year.

Homes are assessed at 19% of market value, and the levy is 5.6600%. Because the tax attaches to the real estate itself, an unpaid balance travels with the house to the next owner, which is why it is cleared at closing. The two sides generally split the year's tax by prorating it, without anyone paying the Collector at the table.

Once the sale is done, send the new owner's name to the Collector's office, 2725 Cantrell Road in Harrisonville, phone 816-380-8377. When your lender pays taxes out of escrow, pass any paper bill you receive along to the lender. Bills are mailed to whatever address sits in the tax file on print day, so a previous owner may still get one.

A parcel left unpaid can be offered at the yearly tax certificate sale in Harrisonville, at the courthouse, starting at 10 a.m. on the fourth Monday of August.

The Recorder reviews, indexes and returns land documents. Staff cannot draft them or help fill them in, so a title company or attorney should prepare the deed.

You can sign up for the county's fraud alert at casscounty.com/fraud to receive a notice if anything with your name on it is recorded. Searching records online is free once you register, and military discharge papers are recorded at no charge. Call the office for the current page charge if you plan to submit a document yourself.

After closing, the deed is the record that makes the new owner's title public. Ask your title company when it will be filed, and keep the settlement statement showing the recording charge.

sections.h2: Getting the house ready to show
sections.html:
Start with the outside, since code enforcement works from the street. Cut the grass, haul off debris and move any vehicle that lacks a plate or has flat tires. Then go through the house for small repairs a buyer would notice, such as loose handrails, dripping faucets and burned-out bulbs.

Next, collect paper. A buyer's lender or title company will want a payoff statement, the latest tax bill and records for any permitted work. Having them in a folder keeps a sale from stalling in the final days before closing.

sections.h2: Questions to put to a buyer
sections.html:
1. What is the full price, and who pays for title, closing and recording?
  2. Is there proof of funds or a lender commitment?
  3. What closing date and move-out terms apply?
  4. Which Cass County title company or attorney will handle the deed?
  5. Have any code notices on the property been cleared?

Gather the latest tax bill and your mortgage payoff figure before you sit down, and ask for two or three bids. On a cash sale, the process is short: the buyer inspects, the title company checks for liens and taxes, you sign the deed and the settlement statement, and the deed is recorded with the county. Ask each bidder to put those steps and dates in writing.

faqs.q: How soon can a Raymore house close with cash?
faqs.a: A cash sale can close once the title search is finished and both sides settle on a date, often within a few weeks. Financing adds an appraisal and a loan underwriting review, so those buyers take longer.
The Raymore-Peculiar R-II School District serves the whole city, so there is just one answer for every address.

faqs.q: What is the due date for Cass County real estate tax?
faqs.a: December 31, with the U.S. postmark deciding timeliness. Call 816-380-8377 if no bill arrives by December 10.

faqs.q: Should I clear code issues before listing in Raymore?
faqs.a: Yes. Tall grass, debris and inoperable vehicles are all enforceable under the property maintenance code, and an open violation can complicate a closing. Call Code Enforcement at (816) 892-3027 to find out what is on file for your address.

faqs.q: Will the Cass County Recorder draft my deed?
faqs.a: No. The office cannot provide or prepare documents for recording, so use a title company or real estate attorney.
